sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa-Australia Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement
Samoa-New Zealand Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement
PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) s. 112; Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2007 (No. 3 of 2007); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2009; Beneficial Ownership (International Companies) Regulations 2020; United Nations Sanctions (Implementation) Act 2015.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent public authority in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; consular legalization required for non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Residential Address (Utility Bill or Bank Statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution, certified by a Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source of Funds/Wealth Disclosure

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and proposed signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit PEP list (FATF Recommendations 12 and 24), the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Samoa's domestic sanctions register administered by the Ministry of Finance. Enhanced due diligence automatically applies where any PEP, family member or close associate is identified, requiring documented source of wealth and source of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry Portal (e-CRS), administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official corporate language for International Companies. Names must be in Latin characters without diacritical marks. A Samoan-language name, if adopted, must be a direct transliteration of the English name. The corporate suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or the Samoan equivalent 'Fa'amasinoga') must be included.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a name rejection, the applicant may submit a written application for reconsideration to the Registrar, attaching the original rejection notice and one to three alternative names. If refused a second time, the applicant may appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days by filing a notice of appeal, the rejection letter, and evidence of marketable distinctiveness. The Minister's decision is final, subject to judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permitted only as a correspondence or service address; a physical registered office in Apia, Samoa, at the office of the licensed registered agent is mandatory. The registered office must display the company name and serve as the location for statutory records, register of members, and minutes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection is 5% for this low-risk online retail entity. The likelihood increases to 10% upon occurrence of a PEP/UBO trigger event, regulatory complaint, or adverse screening flag.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Companies (Fees and Forms) Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International Company incorporation filing and certificate fee
Registered agent and registered office annual fee (local licensed agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an offshore International Company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO and KYC screening package (PEP, UN, OFAC, domestic sanctions)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard CDD bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization bundle per individual
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and apostille-issuing authority in country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark plus government authentication fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and certification of corporate documents and bank references
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for English-language certification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, particularly sections 4 (incorporation), 8 (memorandum of association), 9 (articles of association), 10 (registered office and agent), 19-21 (directors) and 33-36 (share capital and shares)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with the Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for such consideration as the board determines in accordance with section 33 of the International Companies Act. No escrow account is required for an International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation of the Company under the International Companies Act 1987 be confirmed and the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar be adopted. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the subscribers to the Memorandum be and are hereby issued one ordinary share each, fully paid, in accordance with the share subscription register. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Company be fixed at the place designated by the registered agent in Samoa. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole director, [Secretary Name] as company secretary, and [Representative Name] as authorized representative, each to exercise the powers and duties prescribed by the Company's Constitution and applicable law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFSA (e-Registry online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application with up to three proposed company names in order of preference. Pay the prescribed reservation fee and await the Registrar's clearance against existing names and restricted words.
required_dossiers: Certificate of identity of each subscriber (notarized passport or national ID)
Written consent of the proposed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or objectionability, file an alternative name within 5 business days or appeal to the Registrar in writing within 14 days, providing justification and evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, ensure subscriber signatures are notarized or witnessed, and complete the Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1). Submit the full package to the Registry for statutory review.
required_dossiers: Consent of the registered agent to act
Identity and residential address of each subscriber and initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or objection, cure the defect within 30 days by filing amended constitutional documents or supplementary affidavits; pay any reinstatement fee if the file is closed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Registry and the licensed Samoa registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SAMOA-licensed registered agent and designate its office as the Company's registered office. The agent must sign consent and be named in the incorporation submission.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the agent's international company services license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent's consent is invalid or the office address is deficient, appoint a substitute agent and file a notice of change of registered agent/office with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's board of directors (internal corporate action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial director(s) convene and adopt a written first board resolution approving the incorporation, allotment of shares to subscribers, appointment of officers, and adoption of the registered office. Record the allotment in the share register.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of first board meeting (written resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any procedural irregularity in the board resolution may be cured by a subsequent ratifying resolution of the board or by a special resolution of shareholders under section 19 of the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registry confirms compliance, collect the Certificate of Incorporation. File the initial return of directors and registered office (Form IC-2) and, if required, obtain a business license from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for e-commerce trading.
required_dossiers: Business License Application (if physical premise or commercial registration required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certification is delayed or withheld, file a formal follow-up request after 7 business days, escalate to the SIFSA supervisory unit, and seek judicial review under the International Companies Act if necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories is a non-industrial commercial service under the Business License Act 1999 of Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – no operational or manufacturing permit is required for pure e-commerce activity without physical production; a general business license for commercial trading may be obtained from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (Samoa)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – registration only; no full EIA required as the activity involves no manufacturing, processing, or discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or industrial emission thresholds apply. Standard consumer packaging and solid waste handling must comply with the Waste Management Act 2010; e-commerce packaging waste must be disposed through authorized municipal collection services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a leased warehouse or office is used, obtain an occupancy permit and fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority and a structural clearance from the Planning and Urban Management Authority. For a purely virtual office with no physical stock storage, no on-site clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA); online portal: SRA Taxpayer Access Point (TAP)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity intending to carry on taxable activity in Samoa must apply for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the Samoa Revenue Authority. The application is submitted online or in person using Form TIN-01, accompanied by certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, directors' register, and evidence of physical or agent address in Samoa. An International Company (IC) is generally exempt from income tax registration and does not require a TIN for tax-exempt offshore activities, but a TIN and VAGST registration are required if the IC undertakes taxable domestic supplies or imports goods for local consumption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. An International Company is statutorily exempt from all Samoan income, capital-based, and stamp taxes. It may elect to become a domestic ordinary company under the Companies Act 2006, thereby waiving the IC tax-exempt status, but no subchapter-S-style pass-through election exists. No hybrid entity election is available for tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue standard tax invoices containing prescribed particulars; invoices may be paper or electronic. The SRA does not operate an API-based e-invoicing clearance system as of the current stage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated for VAGST when they are exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply, or when they are supplied for use in an export free zone. Offshore services supplied to a non-resident recipient for use entirely outside Samoa are zero-rated. The exporter must hold documentary evidence proving physical export, the recipient's non-resident status, and receipt of foreign consideration. Deliveries to Samoan customers, including online auto-parts sales delivered within Samoa, are taxable at 15% VAGST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims are subject to full VAGST clawback plus interest at the statutory rate. Penalties include a late or false penalty of up to 100% of the tax shortfall and an additional monetary penalty not exceeding WST 10,000 per offence. The SRA may retrospectively audit up to six years and, in cases of wilful evasion, criminal prosecution and director liability may be imposed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; Samoan name: Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) — the sole exchange-control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1983 and the Banking Ordinance 2008; CBS licenses authorised dealers and money remitters, approves non-resident and foreign-currency accounts, issues exchange-control permits, and receives balance-of-payments reporting from commercial banks on all cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed currency without full convertibility. Current-account payments for genuine goods/services are cleared through authorised dealers upon presentation of invoices, contracts and shipping documents, with no CBS pre-approval for standard trade transactions; capital-account flows — equity injections by non-resident shareholders, shareholder loans, dividend repatriations, outward investments and secondary-market securities flows — require CBS notification or prior approval via the authorised dealer. For WS_IC (a non-resident Samoan International Company under the International Companies Act 1987), the optimal classification is an offshore/non-resident entity that settles in USD and avoids unnecessary WST conversion. Dividend/profit remittance hurdles: distributions require (i) audited accounts or the SIFA tax-exempt certificate; (ii) a Certificate of Good Standing; and (iii) a CBS-approved outward dividend form; the hurdle is reduced where the dividend is paid in original foreign currency from a CBS-approved foreign-currency estate, as no WST sale is triggered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa's Exchange Control Regulations require resident exporters to receive and collect export proceeds within six months (180 days) of shipment. Export proceeds invoiced in foreign currency must be surrendered to an authorised dealer and converted to WST at 100% of the receipt value within the settlement windows set by CBS, unless a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or retention approval has been granted in advance. For the ISIC 4791 online aftermarket-parts exporter, the mandated compliance path is to obtain a CBS retention approval through the settlement bank before receiving gateway sweeps, allowing USD platform payouts to be held as USD for direct re-payment of overseas parts suppliers; otherwise every Stripe/PayPal payout is forcibly converted into WST. A structurally non-resident IC conducting pure offshore e-commerce should nonetheless obtain a written authorised-dealer classification confirming it is not a Samoa-resident exporter, in which case the surrender obligation does not apply to its foreign-currency settlement, but supporting documentation of the offshore operating model must be filed with CBS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD multi-currency operational account with segregated capital-injection / escrow sub-ledger
WST operational account for statutory and registered-agent fee payments
WST current account with correspondent-linked foreign-currency facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a collection/payment rail, but never as the settlement bank. Neither Stripe nor PayPal holds a Samoan banking licence; Stripe does not support Samoa as a merchant market, and PayPal permits Samoan merchants only to receive USD credits that must be withdrawn to an authorised-dealer account via SWIFT. Offshore digital EMIs (including Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie and Payoneer) are not licensed by CBS, cannot accept deposits with a Samoan nexus under the Banking Ordinance 2008, do not settle WST, and routinely screen out Samoa International Companies on territorial-availability and e-commerce policy grounds. Legally viable design: use EMI/PSP accounts strictly as pass-through collection wallets from which funds are swept by SWIFT MT103 into the BSP Samoa USD account; the last-mile settlement must always land in a CBS-licensed authorised-dealer account. Any deposit-taking or WST-denominated ledger with an unlicensed EMI would constitute unauthorised banking business under Samoan law.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for directors or ultimate beneficial owners of a Samoan International Company to appear physically in Samoa for account opening; the International Companies Act 1987 requires only a licensed registered agent in Samoa. Banks apply risk-tiered KYC: remote onboarding is permissible where passports and corporate extracts are notarised or apostilled; the registered agent lodges certified company records; and the UBO obtains a banker's or attorney's reference from his home jurisdiction. Most authorised dealers require a recorded video KYC interview with the UBO; where the constitutional documents are in Chinese (中文全中文章程), a certified translation and verified interpreter are mandatory. A physical meeting at the bank in Apia may be imposed as a risk-overlay by the bank's MLRO when the IC's ownership chain is trust-based; this is a bank policy requirement, not a statutory mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company perceived as a shell/letterbox without economic substance in Samoa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; registered-agent due-diligence letter; statutory registers and board resolutions; ISIC 4791 operating plan with live e-commerce marketplace links; platform merchant agreements (e.g., Stripe/PayPal onboarding evidence); UBO and source-of-wealth questionnaire; 12-month cash-flow projection reconciling gateway revenue to inventory purchase obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee directors, Chinese-language constitutional texts or trust-based shareholding obscuring the beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register maintained by the licensed agent; trust deed and trustee/protector identity where a Samoan international trust is the shareholder; notarised identity documents and three-month bank statements for all UBOs; sworn source-of-funds affidavit for initial capital; independent PEP and sanctions screening report; written registered-agent undertaking to notify the bank of any UBO change within 14 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automotive aftermarket parts trade flagged for sanctions, export-control, counterfeit or dual-use exposure across supply chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SKU-level HS/ISIC classification matrix; supplier due-diligence files and country-of-origin certificates; OFAC/EU/UN restricted-party screening results; supporting purchase orders, commercial invoices and transport documents; authenticity and quality certificates from the source supply chain; storefront listing excerpts and returns policy demonstrating genuine retail operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume Stripe/PayPal payout sweeps interpreted as layering or unexplained account turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Order-level transaction logs and platform settlement statements mapped to courier tracking; gateway-to-ledger reconciliation prepared by the external accountant; inventory purchase evidence; chargeback/refund reason-code breakdown; documented treasury policy showing USD receivables held in a USD account and swept to overseas suppliers; independent accountant's report on completeness of revenue capture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border USD funding corridor with payor names inconsistent with declared UBOs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share-subscription or shareholder-loan agreements; bank credit advices and SWIFT remittance purpose codes; corporate registry extracts for any interposed paying entity; group structure chart placing the Samoan IC in the cross-border/trust chain; tax-residency certificates and counterparty bank exchange-control confirmations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol: (1) board resolution approving the equity subscription or shareholder loan; (2) allotment/subscription registered by the SIFA-licensed agent with the Samoan company registry; (3) shareholder bank executes SWIFT MT103 credit to BSP Samoa USD capital sub-account, beneficiary identified as WS_IC; (4) field-70 remittance information must read: /CAP/ subscription under International Companies Act 1987 / capital contribution for online auto-parts trading; (5) sending bank applies BOP/ISO purpose classification of equity capital (code EQU or equivalent); (6) verification package filed with the receiving bank: certified board minutes, application for allotment, registered-agent allotment certificate, source-of-funds evidence and UBO chart; (7) CBS inward-capital declaration is lodged by the authorised dealer where the value exceeds the dealer's exchange-control threshold (plan for review at USD 50,000 per wire); (8) the funds are held in a dedicated USD capital/escrow sub-ledger and released only against documented inventory purchase commitments or platform liquidity needs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement uses two rails. (A) SWIFT MT103 commercial wires for routine prepayment/TT inventory purchases from auto-parts suppliers in China, Japan and the USA; remittance purpose code states 'trade payable — automotive replacement parts', with commercial invoice, purchase-order and dispatch references retained on file; USD clearing runs over the authorised dealer's New York correspondent nostro. (B) Irrevocable commercial documentary letters of credit for bulk sourcing above USD 100,000: issued at sight through BSP (or an offshore issuing bank), requiring seller presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, certificate of origin and inspection certificate; documentary credits settle via SWIFT MT700/MT103/MT202 series. Inward Stripe/PayPal platform sweeps arrive as MT103 credits from the payment processor's payout bank with e-commerce sales purpose coding; those USD receipts must be reconciled at order level in the treasury ledger before being re-disbursed to suppliers. The WST local rail is reserved strictly for domestic statutory fees (registered agent, SIFA annual retention, bank charges) and is not used in the cross-border liquidity spine.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Commercial forward FX contract (USD/WST) — available through an authorised dealer bank only when backed by a documented current-account or approved capital-account exposure; tenor generally up to 12 months; requires CBS authorised-dealer contract registration and underlying trade evidence.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — not offered in the Samoan domestic market and not approved under CBS exchange-control practice; offshore booking requires prior CBS no-objection, otherwise it constitutes unauthorised exchange-control avoidance.

Cross-currency swap (USD/CNY or USD/WST) — permissible on a case-by-case basis as an authorised-dealer-intermediated hedge of maturing trade payables/receivables; the WS_IC must evidence the exact underlying payable or receivable mismatch and the counterparty must be a licensed bank.

Structural USD natural hedge — the primary treasury policy for ISIC 4791 online retail: hold all Stripe/PayPal receivables in the BSP USD account, match USD supplier payables from the same USD estate, and avoid WST intermediation; this is the lowest-compliance-risk liquidity instrument available to the IC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Licence Fee Renewal (no separate annual return is filed for a standard non-regulated International Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via the licensed registered agent; Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of incorporation; the registered agent submits the renewal before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late penalty is imposed on the unpaid annual fee; continued non-payment after formal notice leads to administrative strike-off, and the company may be dissolved if fees remain unpaid for approximately six months

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies to an ordinary exempt International Company in the auto-parts e-commerce sector. Audit is mandatory only for SIFA-regulated licensees (banking, insurance, fiduciary/trust service providers) or if the Registrar directs an audit due to suspected non-compliance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed public accounting framework applies to a non-regulated International Company; internal books may be kept in any recognized accounting format, and IFRS is accepted when voluntary financial statements are prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual renewal, the registered agent obtains written confirmation of current shareholders and beneficial owners; any shareholding transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members promptly, and updated UBO particulars are kept confidential with the registered agent. No public annual UBO filing is made for a standard International Company.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable (audit-exempt); voluntary certified audit approximately USD 4,000 - 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% – International Company (IC) is exempt from Samoan corporate income tax on all offshore-sourced income; the standard domestic corporate rate is 27% (Income Tax Act 2015) but is inapplicable to a compliant IC deriving no Samoan-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 2012 for ICs that do not carry on business in Samoa and derive no Samoan-source income; no capital gains tax; no net wealth tax; no GST/VAT on offshore e-commerce revenue. The annual government licence fee (WST 500–2,000 depending on issued capital) is the only recurring State exaction, effectively replacing income tax for the IC structure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IC-AR (International Company Annual Return) filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) through the registered agent via the eSIFA online portal; no corporate income tax return is lodged for an offshore-exempt IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation; the reporting period is the preceding 12-month period ended on the anniversary date. No audited financial statements are required to be filed for a private IC unless it has opted into the standard taxable regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, registration number, registered agent name and address, registered office address, issued share capital, and principal place of business if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned IC, insert the licensed registered agent's Samoa address as the registered office; state that the principal place of business is outside Samoa and do not list any Samoan operational address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B – Director and Shareholder Register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality, shareholding percentage, and appointment dates of all directors, officers, and shareholders, including ultimate beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders are permitted; provide certified passport copies and proof of residential address to the registered agent. A local Samoan resident director is not mandatory for an IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration that the IC has not carried on business in Samoa, has no Samoan-source income, and has not created a permanent establishment or physical presence in Samoa during the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an auto-parts e-commerce business, confirm that all inventory, fulfilment, and customer-facing operations are located abroad; any Samoan fulfilment centre, employee, or warehouse will negate the offshore declaration and invalidate the tax exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee calculated by reference to issued share capital: up to WST 1,000,000 – WST 500; WST 1,000,001 to WST 10,000,000 – WST 1,000; above WST 10,000,000 – WST 2,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep issued share capital at a minimum initially; additional share issuances can be made by board resolution without reclassifying the IC. The fee is settled by the registered agent from client funds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form IC-AR incurs a penalty of WST 10 per day up to a maximum of WST 5,000; continued default may result in a compliance fine of WST 50,000 or revocation of the IC licence; three consecutive missed filings trigger automatic strike-off by the Registrar of International Companies.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2015 applies only to dividends paid out of Samoan-source profits by a taxable company. A compliant offshore-exempt IC distributing non-Samoan-source profits to non-resident shareholders incurs 0% Samoan dividend WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network; only Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia and New Zealand and participation in the OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance are in force. Treaty relief for dividend, interest, or royalty flows is therefore not available in practice. A Samoan Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) may be requested from the Ministry for Revenue only where the IC demonstrably maintains central management and control in Samoa (board minutes, records, bank account, and local professional substance); shell ICs are routinely refused a TRC. No reduced DTA rate can be invoked where no comprehensive DTA exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan WHT on interest and royalty payments sourced in Samoa is 15% in each category. A fully offshore IC paying for licences, trademarks, software platforms, or intercompany debt out of exempt non-Samoan profits is not subject to Samoan WHT because the payments are not sourced in Samoa; however, the recipient's residence jurisdiction may impose its own tax, and payment routing must not conjure a Samoan source for the obligation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No specific monetary threshold is prescribed in Samoan law for ICs. The transfer pricing rules in the Income Tax Act 2015 apply to related-party transactions only when the IC has opted into the standard tax regime or has derived Samoan-source income. In administrative practice, an IC must maintain transfer pricing documentation when the gross annual value of related-party cross-border transactions exceeds WST 500,000; below this level a light-touch contemporaneous file is recommended.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoan law does not yet impose OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) on International Companies. However, OECD Harmful Tax Practices reviews and European Union listing criteria have created market pressure for ICs to exhibit real substance, including a qualified registered agent, a physical registered office, board records, bank account activity, and accurate payroll or professional service arrangements. A letterbox IC without any demonstrable activity is exposed to financial institution de-risking, foreign tax authority recharacterisation, and treaty denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a material part of the auto-parts e-commerce business in Samoa, such as holding inventory in a Samoan warehouse, employing Samoan personnel, invoicing Samoan customers, or running a Samoan call centre, while continuing to submit the IC offshore declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive cancellation of the IC tax exemption; assessment of Samoan corporate income tax at 27% on all Samoan-source profits for the open tax years; monthly late-payment penalty of 2%; civil penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded under the Tax Administration Act 2017; criminal prosecution in the Supreme Court of Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved or concealed the domestic activity are jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax; the corporate veil may be pierced by court order; Ministry for Revenue may issue distress warrants restricting travel where assets are dissipated; imprisonment of up to 3 years may be imposed for fraudulent tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC as a pure interposed invoice box: no office, no records, no bank account, no board meetings, while the true management and decision-making for the auto-parts e-commerce operations remain entirely in Hong Kong or another offshore centre, and the IC declares offshore status without a genuine business operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off by the Registrar of International Companies for false declarations; disqualification orders barring responsible persons from incorporating in Samoa for up to 5 years; civil penalties on the registered agent up to WST 10,000 for failing to verify beneficial ownership and substance; exposure to OECD and EU listing consequences, which terminate correspondent banking and high-risk payment processing agreements such as Stripe and PayPal accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability to creditors for fraudulent trading; travel bans issued by court order; exclusion orders from Samoa, New Zealand, and Australia under mutual assistance instruments; criminal conviction for perjury if the annual offshore declaration is knowingly false.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or settling payments through Stripe and PayPal where the IC does not identify underlying merchants or beneficiaries, commingles e-commerce revenues with third-party funds, processes chargebacks through stacked duplicate accounts, or involves the movement of proceeds linked to credit-card fraud, counterfeit parts, or consumer deception.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2018 and SIFA directives: fines up to WST 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years for money laundering; freezing orders by the Central Bank of Samoa over all platform payouts; forfeiture of proceeds; cancellation of the IC registration where the company is used as a money-laundering vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control the payment gateways personally can be prosecuted and imprisoned; personal bank accounts linked to the corporate cash flow may be subject to civil forfeiture; Interpol red notices may issue if the activity crosses borders; directors forfeit the benefit of limited liability where fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Indirect Tax Circumvention in the Auto-Parts Market
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing the Samoan IC as entirely tax-free while dispatching automotive replacement parts to consumers in jurisdictions with VAT/GST, sales tax, or customs duties, using the IC to conceal the taxable seller identity and shifting legal liability away from the operating affiliate that controls the platform, warehouse, or merchant-of-record arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign tax authorities may recharacterise the IC as the taxable seller and issue assessments for uncollected VAT/GST, plus penalties of 15% to 100% of the tax due; Stripe and PayPal will permanently terminate the merchant account for misrepresenting business domicile; Samoa may revoke the IC's exemption where the activity is deemed a sham contrary to the offshore declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be added as responsible persons in foreign indirect-tax assessments; travel restrictions may be imposed by issuing jurisdictions for collection enforcement; personal guarantees signed with payment processors expose directors to direct recovery; the corporate veil can be pierced in cases of deliberate misrepresentation.
